questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to derive and implement online statistics for real-time trend detection, emphasizing constant-time per-sample updates and memory efficiency.

## Key Concepts
- **Online (one-pass) statistics**: Computing regression without storing individual data points
- **Running sums**: Maintaining sufficient statistics for linear regression
- **Time-space trade-off**: O(1) updates vs O(n) reprocessing

## Per-Element Update
Each new sample (t, v_t) requires:
```javascript
n     += 1;
sumX += t;
sumY += v_t;
sumXX += t * t;
sumXY += t * v_t;
```

## Memory Usage
O(1) — only five scalar values are stored regardless of the number of samples processed.

## Concrete Example
Suppose sensor values arrive as v_1=3, v_2=5, v_3=7:

| t | v_t | n  | sumX | sumY | sumXX | sumXY |
|---|-----|----|------|------|-------|-------|
| 1 | 3   | 1  | 1    | 3    | 1     | 3     |
| 2 | 5   | 2  | 3    | 8    | 5     | 13    |
| 3 | 7   | 3  | 6    | 15   | 14    | 34    |

After t=3: m = (3·34 - 6·15) / (3·14 - 6²) = (102 - 90) / (42 - 36) = 12/6 = 2, matching the obvious trend v_t = 2t+1.

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to derive an online, numerically stable statistics approach suitable for streaming data with fixed memory.

## Key Concepts
- Online statistics with two accumulators
- Welford’s method for variance stability
- Trade-offs between streaming O(1) memory vs batch recomputation

## Code Example
```javascript
class OnlineStats { constructor(){ this.n=0; this.mean=0; this.M2=0; } add(x){ this.n++; const delta = x - this.mean; this.mean += delta/this.n; this.M2 += delta*(x - this.mean); } variance(){ return this.n<2?0:this.M2/(this.n-1); } stddev(){ return Math.sqrt(this.variance()); } }
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests familiarity with sliding-window analytics, probabilistic sketches, and memory-accuracy trade-offs. The candidate must design a time-bucketed union approach and reason about expirations and error scaling.

## Key Concepts
- Time-bucketed sketches for sliding windows
- HyperLogLog cardinality estimation
- Merging without double-counting across buckets

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudocode sketch usage
let buckets = new RingBuffer(D, new HyperLogLog(m));
for (const id of batch) buckets.current.update(id);
if (timeToExpire()) buckets.evictOldest();
let estimate = unionOfActiveBuckets(buckets);
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you optimize for very high arrival rates?
- How does your choice of D and m affect latency and memory under bursty traffic?
